exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What is Australia’s system of government?
explanation: In a parliamentary democracy citizens vote for people to represent them in parliament. Those representatives must answer to the people at elections.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Australia’s system of government is a parliamentary democracy.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Where does the power of the Australian government come from?
options: From the Australian people, who vote for their representatives
explanation: Citizens vote for people to represent them in parliament. That is why the government’s power is said to come from the people.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: the power of the government comes from the Australian people

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: A religious leader in Australia does not have to obey a law that goes against their religion.
explanation: Under the Rule of Law everyone must obey Australia’s laws. That includes government, community and religious leaders, business people and the police.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: no person, group or religious rule is above the law

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: How do Australians believe change should happen?
options: Through force when a cause is just
Through discussion, peaceful persuasion and the democratic process
explanation: Australians are proud to live in a peaceful country with a stable government. Violence is rejected as a way to change a person’s mind or the law.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: change should occur through discussion, peaceful persuasion, and the democratic process

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What is freedom of association?
options: The right to pay less tax
The right to form and join associations to pursue common goals
explanation: People are free to join any legal organisation, such as a political party, trade union or religious group. They can also decide not to join.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Freedom of association is the right to form and join associations to pursue common goals.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: In Australia a person can be forced to join a trade union.
explanation: Freedom of association includes the freedom not to join. Nobody can be forced into joining an organisation.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: People can also decide not to join, and cannot be forced into doing so.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: The government in Australia is secular. What does that mean?
options: It operates separately from churches and other religious entities
It is led by church leaders
explanation: Australia has no official national religion. The government and the law treat all citizens equally, whatever their religion or beliefs.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: it operates separately from churches or other religious entities

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: A religious practice conflicts with an Australian law. Which one prevails?
explanation: People are free to follow any religion, but the laws of Australia must be obeyed at all times. Where the two conflict, Australian law prevails.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Australian law prevails

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Australia has an official national religion.
explanation: People in Australia are free to follow any religion they choose, or none. The government is secular and has no official religion.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Australia has no official national religion.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What do Australians mean by a “fair go”?
options: Everyone should be paid the same
What someone achieves should come from their talents, work and effort, not their wealth or background
Sport should always be played fairly
The government should give everyone a job
explanation: A fair go is another name for equality of opportunity. It means there are no formal class distinctions in Australian society.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: rather than their wealth or background

subtopic: Responsibilities and privileges of Australian citizenship
question: Which of these is NOT a responsibility of Australian citizens listed in the booklet?
options: Serving on a jury if called
explanation: Citizens must obey the law, vote, defend Australia if needed and serve on a jury if called. Applying for a passport is a privilege, something a citizen can do.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
subtopic: Responsibilities and privileges of Australian citizenship
question: Which of these is NOT a privilege of Australian citizenship listed in the booklet?
options: Serving on a jury if called to do so
explanation: Privileges are what Australia gives a citizen, such as a passport and consular help. Jury service is a responsibility, something a citizen must do.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: As an Australian citizen you can:

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: From what age must Australian citizens vote in federal and state or territory elections?
explanation: Voting is a responsibility, right and privilege for citizens aged 18 or over. It is compulsory in federal and state or territory elections.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: all Australian citizens aged 18 years or over

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What is a referendum?
options: An election for the Prime Minister
An opinion poll run by a newspaper
A vote in a local council
A vote to change the Australian Constitution
explanation: The Constitution can only be changed by the people voting in a referendum. Citizens aged 18 or over must vote in one.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: a referendum, which is a vote to change the Australian Constitution

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: In some states it may not be compulsory to vote in local government elections.
explanation: Voting is compulsory in federal and state or territory elections. Local government elections are the exception in some states.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: It may not be compulsory to vote in local government elections in some states.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What does a jury do?
options: Listens to the evidence in a court case and decides if a person is guilty or not guilty
Decides the penalty for a crime
explanation: A jury is a group of ordinary Australian men and women. Citizens on the electoral roll can be called to serve on one.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: decide if a person is guilty or not guilty

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Service in the Australian Defence Force is compulsory for all citizens.
explanation: Serving in the Defence Force is voluntary. Citizens do have a responsibility to defend Australia should the need arise.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: service in the Australian Defence Force is voluntary

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Who can seek election to parliament in Australia?
options: Citizens aged 18 or over who are not dual citizens
explanation: Standing for parliament is a privilege of citizenship. A candidate must be 18 or over and must not hold another citizenship as well.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: who are not dual citizens, can seek election to parliament

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Which body collects tax in Australia?
explanation: Tax is paid out of the money you earn and is collected by the ATO. Taxes pay for services such as healthcare, education, defence and roads.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: is collected by the ATO

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: An Australian citizen is caught up in civil unrest while overseas. What can they ask for?
options: A trial by an Australian jury
Help from an Australian government official
explanation: Australia has embassies, high commissions or consulates in many countries. Citizens overseas can ask an Australian official for help in times of need.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: you can ask for help from an Australian government official in times of need

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What can Australian citizens do for a child of theirs who is born overseas?
options: Register the child as a permanent resident only
Apply for the child to become an Australian citizen by descent
Apply only if the child returns to Australia to live
explanation: This is one of the privileges of citizenship. Australian citizens can apply for their child born overseas to become a citizen by descent.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: become an Australian citizen by descent
